text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key idea is using clear naming conventions. Variable and function names should describe what they do, so others can follow the logic quickly. Another important point is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes the code simpler to test and change. Clean code also supports maintainability, which means it is easier to fix bugs and add new features later. In short, writing clean code saves time and helps teams work better together.
